column1: # TIME-based SNOBOL4 benchmarks -- MEASURED run-to-run noise floor
#   MACHINE LOAD AT BAKE: nproc=16 loadavg=2.37 1.99 1.37
#   ⛔ THE FLOOR IS A PROPERTY OF MACHINE LOAD, NOT ONLY OF THE ENGINE (s200).  The 2026-08-20 bake ran
#   while EIGHT fleet seats shared this box and its min_detectable reached 47.9% -- a floor that wide
#   cannot see a 1.4x regression.  A solo re-bake of the SAME binaries moved sbl +20.9% and m3 +13.0%,
#   i.e. the shift was LOAD, not the engine and not the oracle flag: -b vs -bf measured back-to-back on a
#   quiet box is -0.3% (+/-2.6%), ZERO.  ⛔ NEVER compare a floor baked under load with one baked solo.
# SCRIP_NOHUGE=1  SCRIP_HEAP_MB=1024  (arena sized past the window so no
#   collection fires inside it -- a GC row measures an ~835ms stall, not dispersion)
# ⛔ THE ALLOCATING ROWS' DISPERSION WAS THE GC STALL LOTTERY, NOT THP (BM-3 correction):
#   whether an ~835ms regeneration lands inside the window is a coin flip, and it was being
#   baked as variance.  GC-free, table_access m3 goes cv 12.4%->1.9% and array_sum 10.9%->0.5%.
# min_detectable_pct = 3*cv; a single-run delta smaller than this is WEATHER.
# ⛔ COLUMNS 1-8 (self.../min_detectable_pct) are the ORIGINAL self-timed TIME() statistic --
#   kept for continuity, still what test_bench_snobol4_timed.sh's live board historically read,
#   but per FINDING-2026-08-22-s253 SPITBOL's TIME() is CPU-time-patched and SCRIP's is wall-clock,
#   so the two were never the same unit.  self(ms) is NEVER AGAIN the cross-engine authority.
# ⛔ COLUMNS 12-17 (elapsed/cpu) are measured by tools/bench_rusage -- ONE external instrument
#   outside both engines, forked around each rep, read via wait4()'s rusage.  A rep whose nivcsw
#   exceeds nivcsw_flag (see header line above) is EXCLUDED from every mean, not averaged in --
#   the mechanical cure for the 47.9% floor.  cpu(user+sys) is the new cross-engine authority;
#   elapsed is reported alongside so min_detectable_cpu_pct and min_detectable_elapsed_pct can be
#   read BY NAME side by side -- cpu should read tighter under load (a descheduled ms counts
#   against elapsed but not against cpu).
#   m4-fixed), sitting beside each kernel's existing TIME-mode triple.  Same columns, same statistics;
#   the only difference is stdin holds the kernel's pinned N (see that script's header) instead of
#   /dev/null, so harness.inc runs fixed-work mode (no calibration, no deadline) instead of TIME mode.
#   reps=3, not 5 -- fixed-work mode has no self-calibration loop to add jitter, so fewer reps already
#   characterize the floor.  MACHINE LOAD AT THIS BAKE: nproc=16 loadavg=2.16 3.23 2.70 (busier than the
#   TIME-mode bake above; several rows -- particularly sbl-fixed on the largest-N kernels, whose longer
#   per-rep runtime is more exposed to preemption -- show every rep nivcsw-contaminated and read NA
#   rather than a number the contamination filter cannot vouch for; see FINDING-2026-08-22-seat2-bench-
#   harness-unmeasurable.md for the callgrind Ir numbers these wall-clock rows do not replace).
